```{r data generation, echo = FALSE, results = "hide"}
AB = sample(1:9,2)*sample(c(-1,1),2,T)
A = AB[1]
B = AB[2]
ex1 = paste0("\\sqrt[3]{x+",A,"}+",B)
ex1 = gsub("+-","-",ex1,fixed=T)
ex2 = paste0("(x+",-B,")^3+",-A)
ex2 = gsub("+-","-",ex2,fixed=T)

inv1 = paste0("x=(y+",-B,")^3+",-A)
inv1 = gsub("+-","-",inv1,fixed=T)

inv2 = paste0("x+",A,"=(y+",-B,")^3")
inv2 = gsub("+-","-",inv2,fixed=T)

inv3 = paste0("\\sqrt[3]{x+",A,"}=y+",-B)
inv3 = gsub("+-","-",inv3,fixed=T)

inv4 = paste0("\\sqrt[3]{x+",A,"}+",B,"=y")
inv4 = gsub("+-","-",inv4,fixed=T)

ach = gsub("+-","-",paste0("\\sqrt[3]{x+",-B,"}+",-A),fixed=T)
ach = c(ach,gsub("+-","-",paste0("\\sqrt[3]{x+",-B,"}+",A),fixed=T))
ach = c(ach,gsub("+-","-",paste0("\\sqrt[3]{x+",B,"}+",-A),fixed=T))
ach = c(ach,gsub("+-","-",paste0("\\sqrt[3]{x+",B,"}+",A),fixed=T))
ach = c(ach,gsub("+-","-",paste0("\\sqrt[3]{x+",-A,"}+",-B),fixed=T))
ach = c(ach,gsub("+-","-",paste0("\\sqrt[3]{x+",A,"}+",-B),fixed=T))
ach = c(ach,gsub("+-","-",paste0("\\sqrt[3]{x+",-A,"}+",B),fixed=T))
ach = c(ach,gsub("+-","-",paste0("\\sqrt[3]{x+",A,"}+",B),fixed=T))

ach = sort(ach)

al = paste0("* $f^{-1}(x)=",ach,"$",collapse="\n")

sol = paste0(1*(ach==ex1),collapse="")

```

Question
========

Let a transformed cubing function be defined by the equation below:

$$f(x) = `r ex2`$$

Find the inverse function.

Answerlist
--------

`r al`



Solution
========

First, get rid of function notation.


$$y = `r ex2`$$

Swap $x$ and $y$ to find an inverse function.

$$`r inv1`$$

Solve for $y$ by undoing the operation on the right side.

$$`r inv2`$$

$$`r inv3`$$

$$`r inv4`$$

The correct answer is $f^{-1}(x)=`r ex1`$.
